name: TRUSS

intro.problem: Neural-network architectures in physics analyses are usually chosen by convention, and there is little evidence that the default topology is the right one once the network must satisfy constraints such as background closure as well as discrimination.
intro.value: A systematic, statistically scored architecture search could find designs that keep discriminating power while modeling background better, and would replace architecture-by-habit with architecture-by-evidence.
intro.approach: We borrow ideas from topology optimization in generative structural design: first calibrate the scale at which adding or removing connections measurably changes performance, then generate candidate topologies from the latent features of trained models and score them on a multi-metric vector, with gates that remove any design that wins by default.
intro.goals: The deliverables are a calibrated sensitivity of performance to connection changes, a set of generated architectures evaluated on seeds disjoint from the search, and a Pareto front showing the real trade-offs among them.

questions: At what granularity of connection changes does performance measurably move?
Can the latent features of trained models seed architectures that outperform the conventional default?
How should architectures be scored so that no design wins by default?
